chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about buying the slaves of the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma) when they acknowledge/endorse that for them. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When they acknowledge that for them, then buy and marry.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying and marrying slaves from the Ahl al-Zimma according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of purchasing slaves from the Ahl al-Zimma (non-Muslims under Islamic protection) provided their status is officially acknowledged, a ruling that underscores the integration of non-Muslim populations within the early Islamic socio-legal framework. The Imam’s addition of 'and marry them' highlights the specific permissibility of contracting marriage with female slaves from this group, reflecting the broader Shia jurisprudence on concubinage and marital unions with 'those your right hands possess.' This ruling is particularly significant in discussions regarding the legal status of slaves in contemporary Shia fiqh and the conditions under which they can be integrated into the Muslim community.
